text.p: Finnish mining and metals group Outokumpu Oy on Monday repeated a forecast that its full-year 1996 result would be considerably weaker than in 1995.
"The result for the financial year 1996 will be considerably weaker than in 1995," Outokumpu said in a statement with its January-August interim report.
"Although the group's financial performance is expected to improve to some extent in late 1996, the result of the last tertial will also be poor," Outokumpu said.
In 1995, the group reported a 1.48 billion markka profit before extraordinaries and tax on net sales of 16.95 billion.

"Despite an anticipated improvement in market conditions, base metals will still post an operating loss for 1996," Outokumpu said, adding: "The business area's profitability is expected to improve in 1997 when cost efficiency reaches target levels following the completion of expansion investments."
"The stainless steel market outlook is troubled by uncertainty. However, demand is (expected) to grow and prices to rise somewhat by the end of the year," it said.
"The outlook for copper products is mainly positive, although market development still involves risks especially in Europe," it said.
Overall economic growth was also expected to speed up in Europe in late 1996, and demand for metals and metal products was expected to strengthen as a result, Outokumpu said.
Outokumpu's eight-month profit before extras and tax slumped over 90 percent to 109 million markka from 1.32 billion.
